name: Biliary Atresia with Splenic Malformation Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for BASM

criteria.description: Persistent neonatal cholestasis with conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
Intraoperative or histological confirmation of obliterated or absent extrahepatic bile ducts
Presence of polysplenia or other splenic anomalies detected by imaging or surgery
Presence of associated congenital malformations such as situs inversus, cardiac defects, or vascular anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent neonatal cholestasis, confirmed biliary atresia, and documented splenic malformation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires surgical exploration and histopathological confirmation; imaging supports identification of splenic and associated anomalies.

searchTerms: persistent bile pigment elevation in infant
neonatal prolonged jaundice with conjugated bilirubin

pathognomonic.notes: Detected by abdominal ultrasound or MRI
searchTerms: polysplenia causing multiple spleen tissue areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or obliterated extrahepatic bile ducts
searchTerms: missing or blocked bile ducts outside liver

common.symptomName: Jaundice persisting beyond 2 weeks of life
searchTerms: jaundice lasting more than two weeks in newborn
persistent neonatal jaundice beyond normal period
acholic stools indicating bile flow problems
heart defects like atrial septal hole
abnormal heart structure present at birth
situs inversus or abnormal organ positioning
signs of increased liver vein pressure
complications from liver blood flow blockage

occasional.symptomName: Vascular anomalies such as interrupted inferior vena cava
searchTerms: abnormal blood vessels like interrupted vena cava

imaging: Ultrasound showing absent or abnormal gallbladder
Polysplenia or multiple splenic nodules on abdominal imaging
Hepatobiliary scintigraphy showing absent bile flow
other: Histopathology showing bile duct obliteration and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: No associated heterotaxy or cardiac anomalies
Presence of splenic anomalies without cholestasis or bile duct obstruction

redFlags: Progressive jaundice with acholic stools in neonate
Rapid onset of liver fibrosis and cirrhosis
Presence of multiple congenital anomalies including cardiac defects and splenic malformations
